original.text: Kusalā dhammā. Akusalā dhammā. Abyākatā dhammā.
original.edition: Mahāsaṅgīti Tipiṭaka (roman script, based on the Sixth Council edition), SuttaCentral bilara-data root/pli/ms; niggahita written ṁ

paraphrase: The matrix opens with the triad of the wholesome: dhammas are wholesome, unwholesome, or indeterminate (neither).

paraphrase: The matrix sets out twenty-two triads (wholesome, feeling, result, clung-to, defiled, applied thought, rapture, to be abandoned by seeing, accumulation, trainee, limited, inferior, fixed destiny, path-object, arisen, past, internal, visible-resistant, etc.) and one hundred Abhidhamma dyads grouped in clusters (roots, taints, fetters, ties, floods, bonds, hindrances, misapprehension, clinging, defilements) by which every dhamma can be classified.
translation_basis: paraphrase made by the unit author from the Pali where the passage was read locally; otherwise from the author's knowledge of the text
notes: Wording read in the local Mahāsaṅgīti root text (bilara-data); paraphrase by the unit author (skeleton phase; fidelity not yet checked). Counts checked locally (22 triads; ten named gocchakas).

original.edition: Mahāsaṅgīti Tipiṭaka (roman script, based on the Sixth Council edition), SuttaCentral bilara-data root/pli/ms; niggahita written ṁ

paraphrase: A further forty-two dyads are taken from the suttas (Suttantika-duka-mātikā), beginning with dhammas that partake of knowledge and those that partake of ignorance.

original.text: Katame dhammā kusalā? Yasmiṁ samaye kāmāvacaraṁ kusalaṁ cittaṁ uppannaṁ hoti somanassasahagataṁ ñāṇasampayuttaṁ rūpārammaṇaṁ vā saddārammaṇaṁ vā gandhārammaṇaṁ vā rasārammaṇaṁ vā phoṭṭhabbārammaṇaṁ vā dhammārammaṇaṁ vā yaṁ yaṁ vā panārabbha, tasmiṁ samaye— Phasso hoti, vedanā hoti, saññā hoti, cetanā hoti, cittaṁ hoti, Vitakko hoti, vicāro hoti, pīti hoti, sukhaṁ hoti, cittassekaggatā hoti,
original.edition: Mahāsaṅgīti Tipiṭaka (roman script, based on the Sixth Council edition), SuttaCentral bilara-data root/pli/ms; niggahita written ṁ

paraphrase: Defines wholesome dhammas by the first sense-sphere wholesome consciousness: whenever a sense-sphere wholesome consciousness has arisen, accompanied by joy and associated with knowledge, with any of the six kinds of object, at that time there are contact, feeling, perception, volition, consciousness, applied and sustained thought, rapture, pleasure, one-pointedness, the faculties, path factors, powers and the other factors listed.
translation_basis: paraphrase made by the unit author from the Pali where the passage was read locally; otherwise from the author's knowledge of the text
notes: Wording read in the local Mahāsaṅgīti root text (bilara-data); paraphrase by the unit author (skeleton phase; fidelity not yet checked).

original.text: Yasmiṁ samaye lokuttaraṁ jhānaṁ bhāveti niyyānikaṁ apacayagāmiṁ diṭṭhigatānaṁ pahānāya paṭhamāya bhūmiyā pattiyā vivicceva kāmehi …pe… paṭhamaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharati dukkhapaṭipadaṁ dandhābhiññaṁ, tasmiṁ samaye phasso hoti, vedanā hoti, saññā hoti, …
original.edition: Mahāsaṅgīti Tipiṭaka (roman script, based on the Sixth Council edition), SuttaCentral bilara-data root/pli/ms; niggahita written ṁ

paraphrase: The supramundane wholesome consciousness is the jhāna developed as the path that leads out and dismantles the round, for abandoning views and reaching the first stage; at that time, besides the jhāna factors, the faculty 'I shall know the unknown', all eight path factors, and calm and insight together are present.
translation_basis: paraphrase made by the unit author from the Pali where the passage was read locally; otherwise from the author's knowledge of the text
notes: Wording read in the local Mahāsaṅgīti root text (bilara-data); paraphrase by the unit author (skeleton phase; fidelity not yet checked).

original.text: Katame dhammā abyākatā? Kusalākusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ vipākā kāmāvacarā rūpāvacarā arūpāvacarā apariyāpannā vedanākkhandho saññākkhandho saṅkhārakkhandho viññāṇakkhandho, ye ca dhammā kiriyā neva kusalā nākusalā na ca kammavipākā, sabbañca rūpaṁ, asaṅkhatā ca dhātu— ime dhammā abyākatā.
original.edition: Mahāsaṅgīti Tipiṭaka (roman script, based on the Sixth Council edition), SuttaCentral bilara-data root/pli/ms; niggahita written ṁ

paraphrase: The indeterminate dhammas are the results of wholesome and unwholesome dhammas in all spheres, functional dhammas that are neither wholesome nor unwholesome nor results, all matter, and the unconditioned element.
translation_basis: paraphrase made by the unit author from the Pali where the passage was read locally; otherwise from the author's knowledge of the text
notes: Wording read in the local Mahāsaṅgīti root text (bilara-data); paraphrase by the unit author (skeleton phase; fidelity not yet checked).

paraphrase: The Dhammasaṅgaṇī's analysis of matter enumerates the great elements and the derived matter (sense faculties, objects, femininity, masculinity, life faculty, intimation, space, lightness, malleability, wieldiness, growth, continuity, ageing, impermanence, edible food) without naming a 'heart-base'.
translation_basis: paraphrase made by the unit author from the Pali where the passage was read locally; otherwise from the author's knowledge of the text
notes: Wording read in the local Mahāsaṅgīti root text (bilara-data); paraphrase by the unit author (skeleton phase; fidelity not yet checked). Local search found no 'hadaya' in the Rūpakaṇḍa; the heart-base is a commentarial identification (see tea:patthana:1.1.2/5).

original.text: Katame dhammā saññojanā? Dasa saññojanāni— kāmarāgasaññojanaṁ, paṭighasaññojanaṁ, mānasaññojanaṁ, diṭṭhisaññojanaṁ, vicikicchāsaññojanaṁ, sīlabbataparāmāsasaññojanaṁ, bhavarāgasaññojanaṁ, issāsaññojanaṁ, macchariyasaññojanaṁ, avijjāsaññojanaṁ.
original.edition: Mahāsaṅgīti Tipiṭaka (roman script, based on the Sixth Council edition), SuttaCentral bilara-data root/pli/ms; niggahita written ṁ

paraphrase: Lists the ten fetters of the Abhidhamma: sensual lust, aversion, conceit, view, doubt, clinging to rules and observances, lust for existence, envy, avarice, ignorance.

original.text: Katame dhammā āsavā? Cattāro āsavā— kāmāsavo, bhavāsavo, diṭṭhāsavo, avijjāsavo.
original.edition: Mahāsaṅgīti Tipiṭaka (roman script, based on the Sixth Council edition), SuttaCentral bilara-data root/pli/ms; niggahita written ṁ

original.text: Katame dhammā nīvaraṇā? Cha nīvaraṇā— kāmacchandanīvaraṇaṁ, byāpādanīvaraṇaṁ, thinamiddhanīvaraṇaṁ, uddhaccakukkuccanīvaraṇaṁ, vicikicchānīvaraṇaṁ, avijjānīvaraṇaṁ.

original.text: Katame dhammā kilesā? Dasa kilesavatthūni— lobho, doso, moho, māno, diṭṭhi, vicikicchā, thinaṁ, uddhaccaṁ, ahirīkaṁ, anottappaṁ.

original.text: Katame dhammā upādānā? Cattāri upādānāni— kāmupādānaṁ, diṭṭhupādānaṁ, sīlabbatupādānaṁ, attavādupādānaṁ.

original.text: Katame dhammā parāmāsā? Diṭṭhiparāmāso. Tattha katamo diṭṭhiparāmāso? Sassato lokoti vā, asassato lokoti vā, antavā lokoti vā, anantavā lokoti vā …
